scenes.script:
Character B says: [Sipping sound]
Character A says: Yemaindhi?
Character B says: Naku... "I got a burning tongue".
Character A says: Adhi "burnt tongue", "burning tongue" kadhu.
Character B says: Enti?
Character A says: "Burning tongue" anedhi oka medical condition. Hot tea thagepudu naluka kalithe, adhi "burnt tongue" avthundhi.
Character B says: Okay okay, naa English chala weak. Matlade tappudu nenu freeze aypothanu.
Character A says: Ayithe nuvvu Supernova app lo Miss Nova tho practice cheyali.
Character B says: AI teacher aa? Kani AI naku ela teach chesthundhi?
Character A says: Ame andariki oke lesson ivvadhu. First nee level ni artham cheskoni, nee kosam oka personalized plan ready chesthundhi.
Character B says: Kani nenu chala mistakes chesthanu...
Character A says: Adhe kadha best part! Nuvvu 1000 mistakes chesina, ame ninnu judge cheyyadhu, 1000 times correct chesthundhi. Inka logic ni nee sontha Telugu lone explain chesthundhi.
Character B says: Chala expensive aa? Naku antha time kuda ledhu.
Character A says: Coaching classes kante chala sasta, roju ki just 15 minutes spend chesthe chalu. Already 1 crore+ Indians confidently ga matladadam nerchukuntunnaru.
Character B says: Wow! Nenu ela join avvali?
Character A says: Install button click chesi, Supernova download chesko, ivvale English matladadam start chey!

parsed.self_critique_fixed: Applied the Telugu-specific gender agreement rule for female subjects: used 'cheyyadhu' and 'ivvadhu' instead of the masculine 'cheyadu/ivvadu'. The hook opens with a natural native Telugu word ('Yemaindhi?'). The quoted English correction lines are preserved verbatim. Code-mixing is applied naturally throughout, avoiding any Sanskritized or textbook-heavy Telugu terminology.
